name: Off-road 4x4
description: A tall, short four-wheel-drive off-roader: Jeeps, Land Cruisers, Broncos and rock crawlers. All four wheels pull, the suspension travels a long way and it sits high, so it climbs what a car can't, but it leans and grips less on the road.
comment: A vehicle preset (#728); see sedan.json for the format. The real car is a 2018 Jeep Wrangler JL Unlimited (4-door) Rubicon 3.6 V6 8-speed automatic with 4.10 axles (#376 step 9c): Car and Driver's test 0-60 mph 7.5 s, 70-0 mph 212 ft, 0.68 g on its mud-terrain tires; Stellantis's spec sheet for the same driveline: 4623 lb curb, 2451/2172 lb front/rear (53/47), 285 hp at 6400 rpm and 260 lb-ft at 4800, 850RE ratios, LT285/70R17 tires (41.5 cm radius, so the final drive is the real 4.10), 3008 mm wheelbase, 1636 mm track, 11.8 m curb-to-curb turning circle. Both axles drive all the time (the real one is part-time 4WD). Its Rock-Trac 4.0:1 low range and Tru-Lok front and rear lockers (open when unlocked, locked rear only or front and rear, only in 4L at 16 km/h or less) are the 2018 JL owner's manual's (pp.318-323; #376 off-road follow-on). The 177 km/h governor, the 6600 rpm limit, the low end of the torque curve, the drag and frontal area, the body's underside (40 cm; the 27 cm clearance is under the axles) and the travel are estimates. Its grip, 1.0, is set between its skidpad and its stop, as the supercar's is: Mantle's tires brake about 1.3 times harder than they corner, where the Rubicon's mud-terrain tires brake about 1.1 times harder (at 1.05, which matched the 0.68 g skidpad, it stopped from 70 in 57.5 m against 64.6). Springs, damping, brakes and engine braking follow steps 7-9's rules: a 1.2 Hz ride, a 0.27 damping ratio, brake torque for the rear to reach its grip, engine braking for about 0.125 g lifting off at 100 km/h.
